open_points.subject: SOURCE_ID_PATTERN
open_points.text: A `source_id` that does not match the imported `SOURCE_ID_PATTERN` constant in full is refused with `invalid_source_id`.
open_points.question: What is the exact value and type of `SOURCE_ID_PATTERN`, and therefore which strings are valid source ids?
options: A compiled full-match pattern accepting exactly 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters
A pattern accepting uppercase as well as lowercase hexadecimal characters
Another closed syntax for source ids
open_points.default_guess: Use a compiled pattern equivalent to `[0-9a-f]{64}` and require a full match.

witness.initial: The token, request form, project id, connection and photo folder are valid; the request carries a 64-character uppercase hexadecimal source_id.
outcomes: A case-insensitive hexadecimal pattern accepts the identifier and continues to the project lock and placement checks.
witness.observer: The caller and any storage backend reached by the accepted request

open_points.subject: M07 PublicationMark.marked_at
open_points.question: Which exact event does `marked_at` denote: receipt of the mark request, completion of validation, acquisition of the project lock, or the instant immediately before the mark record is written?
open_points.default_guess: Use the instant after validation and conflict checking while holding the project lock, immediately before writing the new mark.

witness.initial: A placement exists and has no publication mark.
events: The caller sends a mark request.
The request waits for the project lock before the mark is written.
outcomes: `marked_at` records request receipt, before the wait.
`marked_at` records creation of the mark after the wait.
witness.observer: A caller or administrator reading the persisted PublicationMark

open_points.subject: M07 PublicationMark.marked_at
open_points.text: The calling flow reports the `photo_id` right after `photo.publish` answers, and the deliverer creates the mark.
open_points.question: From what authority does the deliverer obtain the instant written to `marked_at`?
options: A datetime parameter supplied to the mark operation
open_points.default_guess: Use an injected UTC clock port and do not read an ambient clock directly.

witness.initial: A placement exists without a mark; the injected test clock and the host wall clock show different instants.
events: The caller successfully marks the placement.
outcomes: The record contains the instant supplied by the injected clock.
The record contains the host wall-clock instant.
witness.observer: The caller, tests and later readers of the mark record

open_points.subject: M07 PublicationMark.marked_at
open_points.question: What datetime representation must `marked_at` use, including timezone awareness and UTC normalization?
options: A datetime retaining the source clock's offset
open_points.default_guess: Store a timezone-aware datetime normalized to UTC.

witness.initial: The chosen clock represents the same instant with a non-UTC offset.
events: The caller creates a publication mark.
The record is serialized and later read.
outcomes: `marked_at` is normalized to an aware UTC datetime.
`marked_at` is stored without an offset or retains the clock's original offset.
witness.observer: Record readers and equality or ordering checks

open_points.subject: mark operation time readings
open_points.text: The first mark stands when it is sent again, and its `marked_at` does not change
open_points.question: How many times may a mark operation read the decided time source, at which step is it read, and must replayed or conflicting mark calls read it at all?
options: Read exactly once only when a new mark will be written; replay and conflict read zero times
Read once at the start of every mark call
Read at multiple processing stages and use the final reading
open_points.default_guess: Read exactly once, after all checks establish that a new mark will be written; read zero times for replay or publication conflict.

witness.initial: A placement exists; one call will create its mark, followed by a replay of the same photo_id.
events: The caller repeats the same mark request.
outcomes: The clock is read once for creation and not read for replay.
The clock is read at request entry and again during creation or on the replay, despite the stored `marked_at` remaining unchanged.
witness.observer: Deterministic tests and a clock implementation whose reads are observable
